identity.title: Foundations of Equivariant Deep Learning: Unifying Graph and Sheaf Neural Networks

problem.claim: Extend geometric deep learning to richer symmetry structures while covering graph and sheaf neural networks.

gap.claim: No universal approximation theorem was previously known for sheaf neural networks, according to the authors.

contributions.claim: Introduces order-equivariant neural networks (OENN), generalizing graph message passing and sheaf neural networks through equivariant bundles over face posets/categories.
Characterizes all linear order-equivariant maps, constructs OENN layers, and states universal approximation theorems for continuous order-equivariant maps.
Extends the framework to category-equivariant neural networks (CENN) for categorical, potentially non-invertible symmetries with compositional relations.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that their universal approximation results are new even for sheaf neural networks, where they report no prior UAT was known.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report universal approximation theorems for continuous order-equivariant maps.
The authors report that the framework extends the known graph-neural-network UAT to a setting that also subsumes sheaf neural networks.
The authors report illustrating the framework on graph and sheaf models.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames symmetry-aware geometric deep learning as a way to improve deep-learning performance and efficiency.
It proposes OENN to exploit richer order-based symmetries and unify graph message passing with sheaf neural networks.
It characterizes linear equivariant maps, builds layers, and provides universal approximation theorems, including a reported new result for sheaf networks.
It relates the results to graph UATs, illustrates graph and sheaf models, and extends the framework to categorical symmetries through CENN.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns a generalized architecture with structural theory and approximation guarantees, then situates it relative to graph and sheaf models.

lessons.interpretation: A transferable research pattern is to make the scope extension explicit while pairing the new model with formal characterization and claim-specific guarantees.
lessons.application: When proposing a broader symmetry-aware architecture, define the inclusion relation to existing model classes, state the corresponding formal guarantee, and demonstrate representative inherited cases.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the work has no formal theory or when the proposed system does not genuinely subsume the cited model classes.

unknowns: The abstract does not state the assumptions, domains, or exact formulations of the approximation theorems.
The graph and sheaf illustrations lack datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results.
The abstract does not specify the precise additional capabilities or evaluations of CENN.
